newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda takes new measures to end insecurity.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda takes new measures to end insecurity.

text.p: Rwanda said on Friday it was taking new measures against an upsurge of violent attacks that the government blames on Hutu former soldiers and militiamen.

State radio quoted Foreign Minister Anastaza Gasana as telling foreign diplomats in the capital Kigali that as well as pursuing those responsible for attacks the government would launch a re-education programme for former soldiers.
"The government is in the process of dealing with this situation," Gasana was quoted by the radio as saying.
The radio also quoted an army spokesman as saying a campaign would soon be launched to persuade local people against collaborating with the armed opposition groups.
Hundreds of people as well as at least six expatriates have been killed in Rwanda in the last two months, prompting foreign aid agencies to pull their foreign staff out of western Rwanda.
The government blames Hutu former troops and militiamen who returned home among more than a million refugees who returned home in the last two months of last year from Tanzania and Zaire.
The refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The Foreign Correspondents Association of East Africa meanwhile said it noted with dismay the February 10 expulsion from Rwanda of Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings.
In a letter to the office of the president in Kigali, the Nairobi-based association said it hoped the government of Rwanda would continue to make it possible for foreign journalists to do their jobs.

Jennings was expelled following a report that misquoted military strongman Major-General Paul Kagame as saying Rwanda had the right to divert some foreign aid to help the internal war against Hutu extremists.
